toegepas.blok: Genoeg, en nie te veel nie
toegepas.rede_vinder: Coming straight after the sentence about fats, sugar and salt, a bare 'Hoeveel' can be read as how much of those; naming 'kos' removes the doubt without adding content.
toegepas.fout: bare 'Hoeveel' straight after the fats, sugar and salt sentence can be read as how much of those
toegepas.rede_keurder: Naming 'kos' removes the doubt about what the amount refers to without adding content or touching a protected wording.

toegepas.voor: met vleis en suikerbone en drink water
toegepas.na: met vleis en suikerbone, en hy drink water
toegepas.rede_vinder: Two 'en' in a row lets 'suikerbone en drink water' run together; giving the second clause its own subject makes it clear and takes the AWS comma.
toegepas.fout: 'suikerbone en drink water' runs the list into the second verb, so the reader stumbles on first reading
toegepas.rede_keurder: Giving the second clause its own subject with the AWS comma makes the sentence read cleanly, keeps 'suikerbone' and leaves the meaning unchanged.

toegepas.voor: as wat dit gebruik en stoor die res as liggaamsvet
toegepas.na: as wat dit gebruik. Dit stoor die res as liggaamsvet
toegepas.rede_vinder: In one sentence 'gebruik en stoor' reads as two verbs inside the comparison clause; splitting it shows that storing the rest is what the body does, and keeps 'die res' as the reviewer ruled.
toegepas.fout: 'as wat dit gebruik en stoor' can be read as both verbs sitting inside the comparison, which says something different
toegepas.rede_keurder: Splitting the sentence shows that storing the rest is what the body does, keeps 'meer energie uit enige kos' and 'die res' intact, and is easier for a Grade 6 reader.

laat_vaar.na: en mis die vitamien C daarin
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'hulle' can point back to 'vitamiene en minerale' earlier in the sentence; 'daarin' ties the vitamin C to the fruit and vegetables and avoids the double negative of the earlier dropped proposal.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'hulle' already points naturally to the fruit and vegetables just named, and 'daarin' could just as well point back to 'sy kos', so this is a lateral move with its own ambiguity.

na_skrywer.voor: Vesel kom uit kos van plante soos
na_skrywer.rede_vinder: As it stands 'soos vrugte, groente, boontjies en bruinbrood' attaches to 'plante', so it says fruit and brown bread are plants; 'plantkos' makes the examples refer to the food.
na_skrywer.fout: 'soos vrugte, groente, boontjies en bruinbrood' can attach to 'plante', listing brown bread as a plant
na_skrywer.rede_keurder: The attachment fault is real, but 'plantkos' commonly means fertiliser in Afrikaans, which moves the meaning in a subject that also teaches nutrients in soil for plants, so the writer must fix it another way.
na_skrywer.waarom: the reviewer sent it to the writer
